hints: The gradient of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration.
From rest to $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with acceleration $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ takes time $T = \frac{20}{2}$.
walkthrough:
Use the acceleration formula or gradient of the first segment:
$$a = \frac{v - u}{T}$$
$$2 = \frac{20 - 0}{T} \implies T = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall that the gradient of a velocity-time graph equals the constant acceleration:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$$

The car accelerates from $u = 0$ to $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in time $T$ at rate $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$2 = \frac{20 - 0}{T}$$
$$2 = \frac{20}{T}$$

Multiply by $T$ and divide by $2$:
$$T = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ s}$$

hints: Express the distance travelled before constant speed begins as the area of a triangle ($0$ to $10\text{ s}$) plus a trapezium ($10$ to $15\text{ s}$).
Express the distance travelled from when constant speed begins as the area of a rectangle ($15$ to $42.5\text{ s}$) plus a triangle ($42.5$ to $47.5\text{ s}$).
Set the first distance equal to one third of the total distance (or one half of the second distance) and solve for $V$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the distance travelled before constant speed begins:
$$s_1 = \frac{1}{2}(10)(20) + \frac{1}{2}(20 + V)(5) = 100 + 50 + 2.5V = 150 + 2.5V$$

Calculate the distance travelled during and after constant speed:
$$s_2 = 27.5V + \frac{1}{2}(5)(V) = 27.5V + 2.5V = 30V$$

State the relationship given in the problem: $s_1 = \frac{1}{3}(s_1 + s_2)$, which implies $s_1 = \frac{1}{2}s_2$:
$$150 + 2.5V = \frac{1}{2}(30V)$$
$$150 + 2.5V = 15V$$
$$12.5V = 150$$
$$V = \frac{150}{12.5} = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Recall that distance travelled on a velocity-time graph equals the area under the curve.

Split the journey into stages:
Stage 1 (acceleration from $0$ to $10\text{ s}$): triangular area
$$\text{Area}_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 20 = 100\text{ m}$$
Stage 2 (deceleration from $20$ to $V$ over $5\text{ s}$): trapezium area
$$\text{Area}_2 = \frac{1}{2}(20 + V) \times 5 = 50 + 2.5V$$
Total distance before constant speed begins:
$$s_{\text{before}} = 100 + 50 + 2.5V = 150 + 2.5V$$

Stage 3 (constant speed $V$ for $27.5\text{ s}$): rectangular area
$$\text{Area}_3 = 27.5V$$
Stage 4 (deceleration to rest over $5\text{ s}$): triangular area
$$\text{Area}_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times V = 2.5V$$
Distance travelled after constant speed begins:
$$s_{\text{after}} = 27.5V + 2.5V = 30V$$

The problem states that $s_{\text{before}}$ is one third of total distance $s_{\text{total}} = s_{\text{before}} + s_{\text{after}}$:
$$s_{\text{before}} = \frac{1}{3}(s_{\text{before}} + s_{\text{after}})$$
$$3 s_{\text{before}} = s_{\text{before}} + s_{\text{after}}$$
$$2 s_{\text{before}} = s_{\text{after}}$$
Substitute the expressions for $s_{\text{before}}$ and $s_{\text{after}}$:
$$2(150 + 2.5V) = 30V$$
$$300 + 5V = 30V$$
Subtract $5V$ from both sides:
$$25V = 300$$
Divide by $25$:
$$V = \frac{300}{25} = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
